title: Building a New Future
coreMove: Build the new future by treating the calmest self as a behavioral template: use its clues, repair old fear, choose principles, and repeat one microshift today.

exampleSpecs.audience: Irina, a project lead feeling pulled toward a calmer work life
exampleSpecs.stakes: The highest potential future self exercise has to become present conduct, not a fantasy board.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn the 5 years image and keys exercise into one behavior today.

exampleSpecs.audience: Weston, a parent noticing old fear during conflict
exampleSpecs.stakes: Inner child work has to include the younger self rather than shame him for still needing protection.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Sheri Jacobson's Harley Therapy frame to guide a younger part.

exampleSpecs.audience: Eileen, a manager whose promotion went to someone else
exampleSpecs.stakes: Principles have to steady conduct after an outcome refuses to cooperate.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anchor action in Stephen Covey and Benjamin Hardy rather than trying to control results.

exampleSpecs.audience: Finley, an adult tracing a fear response through generations
exampleSpecs.stakes: Intergenerational trauma can explain fear without making repair impossible.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Martha Henriques's BBC 2019 question to choose safety work instead of denial.

exampleSpecs.audience: Diogo, a founder trying to stop proving worth through exhaustion
exampleSpecs.stakes: Future-self embodiment has to expand the comfort zone without shocking the system.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a small repeated choice creating evidence for a new identity.

exampleSpecs.audience: Neha, a designer rebuilding trust after a breakup
exampleSpecs.stakes: The keys exercise has to yield concrete commitments across 7 years, not mystical certainty.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the 7 years symbolic exchange to identify present commitments.
